四级核心词汇 · 09英文原文

The Door the Vote Forgot

投票时被忘记的那扇门 · 589 词 · 9 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1An elected municipal council planned to turn a vacant hall into a community center. Candidates in a local election had pledged to support it. A preliminary poll showed a clear majority in favor. Rosa, a resident who used a wheelchair, asked which door visitors could use. The draft policy reserved the broad entrance for staff. It won approval in principle before anyone checked the narrow public door. The council had never debated who could get through it.

2A conservative deputy said the plan complied with the applicable code. Rosa asked the council to read the rule aloud. It set a fundamental safety standard. Adoption of a more inclusive plan could promote equality. An advocate from a welfare organization said the decision affected a minority seldom present at meetings. The chair asked her to submit a specific proposal. An independent panel would comment on it before the next ballot.

3A committee member opposed the change on grounds of cost. Another wanted to ban all private events. The chair asked both to refrain from making new demands until a survey was complete. The broad door already had a level path. A short ramp was needed inside. The main obstacle was a cupboard behind the door. The report clarified how the town could advance the plan.

4A campaigner circulated a message saying the initiative granted a particular group a privilege. Rosa invited him to visit with a parent who pushed a stroller and a veteran with a weak leg. They could all use the same entrance. Equal access was a basic provision. The visitor withdrew his criticism and proposed a large sign. An hour at the hall persuaded him to support the reform. The debate remained civil.

5At a forum, citizens debated how a recreation center could serve diverse groups. A resident wanted to impose a permanent time limit on noisy parties. A secretary recorded the complaints and a possible compromise. The council would publish its hours and then assess the overall effect. It asked a neutral environmental officer to coordinate the review with nearby residents.

6A newspaper called the dispute a test of local democracy. One reader asked why the town did not wait for parliament to legislate on public buildings. The council's lawyer explained that a local authority already had a framework for approving changes. He distinguished that power from federal rules. The town could undertake the work without waiting for a new law.

7The campaign reopened a wider controversy. How could a democratic meeting hear those who could not attend? A representative of the night shift suggested an afternoon session. Its first comments helped the council resolve the timing problem. Each group could state its needs. The council could revise the hours if necessary.

8On voting day the council added a line to its resolution. Both doors could be used, but public events had to keep the broad one clear. The majority voted to abolish the old restriction. A deputy who had first opposed it volunteered to implement the decision. His priority was to make the opening notice specify the route from the nearest avenue.

9When the hall opened, the mayor invited Rosa to give a speech. She took the opportunity to ask the guests to walk beside her. They passed the old cupboard, now downstairs. A child asked whether the town had made a new door. Rosa pointed to the familiar handle. A small repair and a new rule had strengthened everyone's right to enter. The council's report made a member of staff accountable for keeping it open.

四级核心词汇 · 09中文译文

投票时被忘记的那扇门

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1民选的市议会想把一座空置大厅改成社区中心。地方选举的候选人承诺支持这项计划，初步民调也显示，多数人明确赞成。使用轮椅的居民罗莎问，来访的人能走哪扇门。政策草案把宽门留给了工作人员。大家原则上通过方案时，还没人检查那扇窄窄的公众入口。议会也从没谈过，谁能顺利通过那道门。

2一位保守派议员说，方案符合适用的建筑规定。罗莎请大家把条文念出来。那条规定设的是基本安全标准，采纳更包容的方案同样可行，也能促进平等。一位福利机构的倡议者说，这个决定影响到一群很少能来开会的人。主席请她提交具体建议，交给独立小组在下次投票前给出意见。

3一位委员嫌改动太贵，另一位想禁止所有私人活动。主席请两人等调查完成再提新要求。宽门外已经有一条平整的路，门内只缺一段短坡道。真正挡路的是门后那只储物柜。调查报告把镇上可以怎样推进这件事说清楚了。

4一位活动人士转发消息，说新做法会给某一群体特殊待遇。罗莎邀他来看看，同来的有推婴儿车的家长，还有一位腿脚不便的退伍军人。他们三个人都能用同一个入口。能平等进门是最基本的安排。来访者收回批评，还建议做个大字标牌。在大厅里走了一小时，他转而支持这项改革，双方也一直保持了礼貌。

5在公共论坛上，居民讨论活动中心怎样服务不同的人。一位居民想给吵闹的聚会定个长期有效的结束时间。秘书记下意见和可能的折中办法。议会准备先公布开放时间，再看整体效果，并请一名中立的环境事务人员和附近居民一起做这项评估。

6报纸把争论称为对地方民主的一次考验。有人问，镇上为什么不等议会为公共建筑专门立法。市议会的律师解释，地方当局已经有批准改动的程序。他把地方权力和联邦规则作了区分。镇上可以先做这项工作，不必等新的法律通过。

7这场活动又引出一个更广的问题。无法到会的人，怎样才能在民主会议上被听见？一位夜班人员的代表建议加开一场下午会议。那次会议一开始收到的意见，就帮议会解决了时间安排问题。各群体可以说出自己的需要，必要时议会还能调整开放时间。

8投票当天，议会在决议里加了一行。两扇门都可以用，举行公共活动时，宽门必须保持畅通。多数人投票取消旧限制。一位起初反对的议员主动来执行这项决定。他先要做的是在开门通知里写清楚，从最近的大街怎么走过去。

9大厅开放时，市长请罗莎讲话。她借这个机会请来客和她一起走过去。他们经过已经搬到楼下的旧柜子。一个孩子问，镇上是不是装了一扇新门。罗莎指指那个熟悉的门把手。一处小修缮、一条新规定，让每个人都有了更可靠的进门权利。议会也在报告里明确了由谁负责保证门一直开着。
